findings.claim: The mixins pass values unchanged to legacy properties. `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` need start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end, so a call like align-items(flex-start) would emit invalid legacy CSS.

verifier.reason: The new `align-items` mixin in app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:137-143 passes `$alignment` unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, so `flex-start` or `flex-end` would produce invalid legacy values. findings.claim: The order mixin passes `$val` directly to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Those legacy properties are 1-based, while `order` is 0-based, so ordering in older WebKit/Firefox is off by one, and a value of 0 is invalid.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `@mixin order($val)` at app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125-131. It passes `$val` unchanged to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group`. Those legacy properties count from 1 and default to 1, while `order` defaults to 0, so `order(0)` would give an invalid value. The only current callers are `order(3)` in header.scss:39 and `order(2)` in topic.scss:30. Both are positive, so their order relative to default items stays correct.

findings.claim: The align-items() mixin emits no `-moz-box-align`, although flexbox() emits `display:-moz-box`. Old-box-model Firefox therefore stretches items instead of centring them.

Old-box-model Firefox would therefore fall back to the default box-align of stretch. Only very old Firefox (before 22/28) is affected, because later versions use the `display: flex` declared after it.
